chunks: My father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir al-Bajali and al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habib, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said in the illness in which he passed away: 'Call for my friend.' So Aisha and Hafsa sent for their fathers. When they came, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) covered his face and head, so they returned. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) uncovered his head and said: 'Call for my friend.' So Hafsa sent for her father and Aisha sent for her father. When they came, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) covered his face. So they went away and said: 'We do not think the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) wanted us.' They said: 'Yes, he only said: Call for my friend' or he said: 'Call for my beloved,' so we hoped that you two were the ones. Then the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) came to him. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) pressed his chest to his chest and gestured to his ear, and he narrated to him one thousand narrations, each of which has one thousand chapters.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad whisper to Imam Ali during his final illness?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) distinguishes between the general companions, represented by the fathers of Aisha and Hafsa, and his specific spiritual heir, Imam Ali (peace be upon him), by concealing the former and embracing the latter. This act of *takhassus* (specialization) underscores the Shia belief that Ali alone received the comprehensive, esoteric knowledge (*'ilm*) necessary for guiding the community after the Prophet's death. The 'one thousand narrations, each with a thousand chapters' symbolizes the infinite depth of divine wisdom transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-42 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father, Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Valeed and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Bashir al-Bajaly and al-Hassan ibn Fazal, on the authority of Al-Masni ibn al-Valeed al-Han’nat, on the authority of Mansoor ibn Hazim, on the authority of Bakr ibn Habib, on the authority of Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB), “

When God’s Prophet (MGB) was so ill that he (MGB) was about to die, he (MGB) said, ‘Call in my friend.’ Then both Ayesha and Hafasa sent someone after their fathers (Abu Bakr and Umar). When they came in, God’s Prophet (MGB) covered up his face. Then Abu Bakr and Umar returned. Then the Prophet (MGB) uncovered his face and said, ‘Call in my friend.’ Again both Ayesha and Hafasa sent someone after their fathers - Abu Bakr and Umar. When they came in, God’s Prophet (MGB) covered up his face again. Then Abu Bakr and Umar said ‘We do not think that God’s Prophet (MGB) wants to see us.’ Ayesha and Hafasa said ‘When the Prophet (MGB) said ‘Call in my friend’ we hoped that he (MGB) wants to see you.’ Meanwhile the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) came in. When the Prophet (MGB) saw Ali (MGB), he hugged him and whispered one-thousand narrations to him each of which has one-thousand chapters.”
